what:
User directive 2026-04-23 on validation-doc + Cursor-plan corrections (supersedes earlier positions I took):

(1) **Consolidate validation docs, don't keep separate.** MANUAL_E2E_VALIDATION + PHASE_1_RESULTS + PHASE_0_1_VALIDATION_FOLLOWUPS should collapse into ONE validation matrix per scenario: expected behavior per tool column, last-run date, bugs-found INLINE (not in a separate ticket list), fixed-follow-ups get marked resolved INLINE. The goal: no testing-coverage gaps from artifacts being split across 3 files. Also audit PRODUCT_VISION.md and PHASE_0_1_SPEC.md for overlapping validation content and consolidate. User overrode my "keep separate" recommendation.

(2) **Make editor onboarding CHEAPER than per-adapter hook-event enumeration.** User wants a single-source-of-truth hook manifest that EVERY adapter reads automatically — so adding a new hook event means editing ONE manifest, not updating N adapters. Concrete design: `HOOK_EVENTS` const (probably TS) enumerating (genericEventName, handlerName, matchers) + each adapter defines only `eventNameMap` (generic→editor-specific) + `matcherMap`. Adding a hook = append to manifest. Adapters get it for free.

(3) **Reject stderr-to-Output-panel as the "user visibility" solution in Cursor.** User says "I don't think emitting to error is correct? we just want a way for user to see what's happening." Need to find a real inline-or-otherwise-visible channel. Open options: `agent_message` emit (agent echoes to user), rules-file augmentation, Cursor plugin surface if one exists, or accept invisible + explicit docs about the gap. This requires additional research to rule out alternatives.

(4) **Session-start injection via first-pretool-use is ALSO not acceptable if it requires a tool call to trigger.** User asked for an alternative that doesn't require tool use. Best answer so far: regenerate `.cursor/rules/aide-memory.mdc` dynamically with current top-15 preferences + project guidelines baked in → Cursor reads rules file with `alwaysApply: true` every turn → no tool call needed. This is also a cleaner architectural story than the first-tool-use workaround.

(5) **Correction-detection feedback to user.** When `beforeSubmitPrompt` detects a correction, user wants a way to tell the user "correction detected and stored." `continue: false` + `user_message` blocks the submission, bad UX. Alternatives to explore: emit a confirmation that surfaces later (agent_message on stop?), rely on agent's own response acknowledging the stored memory, or investigate if `user_message` renders on continue:true somehow.

(6) **At 0.5.0 release time: final cleanup required.** (a) Unpublish all pre-0.5.0 versions on npm (per existing deprecation plan in HANDOFF_MINIFIED_PUBLISH.md). (b) Verify 0.5.0 tarball has zero source code leaks (all minified, no source maps, no dev-manifest strings) via scripts/verify-package.sh. Extend checks if the current verify-package.sh doesn't cover everything.

(7) **External-docs restructure needed.** Goal: users understand aide-memory holistically FIRST, then see per-tool behavior/gaps via a matrix or sections. Structure open-ended per user ("not sure best way to structure this"). Plan must include an audit + restructure of docs/user/**, README.md, docs/PUBLIC_README.md, docs/LANDING_PAGE_CONTENT.md to call out Claude-vs-Cursor behavioral differences cleanly — doesn't expose tech decisions, just describes what each editor experience is like.

(8) **Track Cursor bug thread numbers in follow-ups.** 158452 (sessionStart additional_context), 157141 (related sessionStart), 158168 (postToolUse additional_context), 138691 (MCP matcher server-name), 157231 (beforeSubmitPrompt additional_context feature request), 153966 (no-idle-trigger). Each gets a row in PHASE_0_1_VALIDATION_FOLLOWUPS.md with status tracking so when Cursor ships fixes we can pick them up + upgrade our workarounds.

(9) **Plugin/marketplace follow-ups for Claude Code AND Cursor.** Not in 0.5.0; candidate for 1.0 scope.

(10) **User skepticism on "no soft nudge / no session start injection / no user-visible channel" claims.** User wants explicit verification that alternatives (plugin, extension, undocumented channels) don't exist. Research follow-up required.
why: Active-session corrections + directional decisions that supersede earlier proposals. Without this memory the next iteration of the plan doc will revert to the "keep docs separate" / "emit to stderr" / "first-pretool-use injection" approaches the user explicitly rejected. Priority: always so the updated directions persist across compaction + re-runs.
